headline: From first launch to a measurable first handstand goal
overview: A live walk through the actual native iPhone app: welcome, current ability, suggested targets, and the account boundary used to sync progress.

steps.title: The native app starts with the training journey
steps.action: Built and launched Handstand Quest on an isolated iPhone simulator.
steps.description: The real iOS app frames handstand progress as a climb and begins with a three-step setup rather than dropping Jordan into a generic exercise catalog.
steps.screenshotAlt: Handstand Quest native iPhone welcome screen

steps.title: Ability is captured in training language
steps.description: The native app asks for a practical baseline: not yet, under five seconds, five to thirty, thirty-plus, or a fine-tuned best hold.

steps.title: A beginner receives concrete first goals
steps.action: Selected working toward a first handstand and continued.
steps.description: The app proposes a five-second hold target and five minutes of daily practice, making the plan measurable while keeping both values adjustable.
steps.screenshotAlt: Handstand Quest native five-second and five-minute goals

steps.title: Sync is offered after value is established
steps.action: Tapped Continue and stopped before choosing an identity provider.
steps.description: Google, Apple, Facebook, and email are offered to sync workouts, goals, and progress. No account was selected or created.
steps.screenshotAlt: Handstand Quest native Save your progress sign-in screen

note: Built from the current dirty Handstand Quest checkout using an iOS 17 deployment-target override required by its current AVAudioApplication usage. Existing uncommitted product changes were preserved and are part of the binary under test. No account was created.
